subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm deciding whether to keep the model static or add a minimal joint rig for the turret and barrel, leaning toward a simple hull-turret joint hierarchy rather than a full creature-style rig.

Now I'm sketching out the overall proportions for the vehicle: a roughly 9-meter hull, six wheels in a typical 6x6 configuration, a cab at the front, and a railgun assembly mounted on the rear deck angled forward over the cab, along with deployable stabilizer outriggers braced against the ground. I'm also planning a reusable box-building helper function and picking a military color palette of olive and dark grey panels for the armor plating.

Building the hull and wheel joints...

Now I'm planning the chassis structure—a lower frame box, fender covers over the wheels, and an upper hull deck, all defined in world coordinates attached to the hull bone. I'm setting up a box-building helper function to streamline part creation, then starting to lay out the frame dimensions.

Adding more hull parts...

Positioning the windscreen plane along the slope with proper orientation and texturing it with a glare-visor effect. Then I'm extruding the rear deck hull from a profile with panelled olive paint matching the cab, adding the chassis lower box, and building wheel arch fenders as small boxes positioned at each wheel's side.

I'm working out wheel geometry: centering wheels at y=0.65 with radius 0.65 so the top sits at 1.3, aligning fender height and width to clear the hull edges, and spacing three axles front-to-back (around z=3.0, 0.3, -2.4) so the rear axle sits under the railgun. I'm also adding axle cylinders through each wheel pair, a differential box, and lowered wheel arch cutouts along the hull sides.

Now I'm checking whether the hull half-width overlaps the wheels and deciding to shift the wheel centers outward to x=1.75 so the fenders (1.4 to 2.1) clear the 2.9-wide hull cleanly, then connecting the hubs with a longer axle. I'm also planning four stabilizer outrigger legs, positioning the front pair between the first and second axle gaps and the rear pair further back, checking wheel radius clearance so the legs don't collide with the tires.

Writing leg geometry code...

Still working out turret geometry...

Adding glow strips and insulator spacer clamps along the rails...

Now I'm placing the breech block as a large box behind the rails, then adding capacitor banks as stacked glowing cylinders on either side of the rear deck, connected to the breech with dark cable sweeps, and starting on a muzzle end brace.

Next I'm checking the barrel's geometry at full extension against the cab and pivot point to confirm clearance and overall vehicle height, then moving to the cradle's trunnion support pillars on the turret.

Checking the breech end clearance against the deck, I realize the rear overhangs into the deck top, so I shorten the breech's position along u to keep its underside above 2.3. With that adjustment the turret body region and breech no longer overlap awkwardly, so this geometry works.

Now I'm sketching the elevation actuator as a hydraulic cylinder running from the turret rear to the gun's underside, plus cab details like headlights, bumper, mirrors, roof lamp bar, antenna, a small radar dish, door decals, and twin exhaust stacks behind the cab with elbow caps. I still need to add rear tow hooks, lights, a ladder, and a fuel door.

I'm also planning side stowage boxes above the fenders and working out a procedural camouflage paint scheme using layered noise functions to blend olive, dark olive, and tan patches, then wrapping it in a riveted panel texture for added surface detail.

For decals, I'm sketching out hazard stripes for the leg beams and bumper, a tinted visor-style windshield with highlights, a unit insignia emblem for the cab and turret, warning text for the capacitors, and a rear number plate, all applied via a texture-plane decal helper.

Now I'm positioning emblem and door decals on the cab sides using mirrored offsets and direction vectors so the text reads correctly from outside, then moving into wheel detailing—tire, hub, hub cap, and lug bolts arranged radially on the outer face.

Still working out tire geometry...

I should also add underbody details like drive shaft rods, differential spheres, and mudflaps behind the rear wheels, plus a skirt piece. Aiming for around 250 parts total, I'll define a color palette (olive, tan, steel, iron, black tire, hazard yellow, cyan, orange, red) and bring in a glow effect kit for accents before writing the full code.

Setting up imports and a camo paint function that blends olive, dark olive, and tan based on layered noise, lightening tops based on surface normal...

Still writing helper constructors...

Now I'm setting up the gun frame geometry, defining the elevation angle and direction vectors for the gun's pivot point, with a helper function to compute positions along the gun's axis using these direction vectors.

Skipping recoil slide for now, I'm placing glow strips just inside the rail inner faces, thin boxes running the rail length positioned near x ±0.2.

I'm leaving the armature gap open but adding a faint cyan glow line at the bottom center channel, and spacing out dark steel clamps along the rail length as bridging elements over the gap.

Making the rails copper-colored for contrast against the glow, then designing the muzzle end with top and bottom plates plus a glow ring, and sizing the breech box at the rear end of the rail assembly with proper position calculations.

I'm adjusting pivot height so the turret clears the deck, then laying out the trunnion pillars and turret body dimensions, settling on a ring cylinder and rotating turret box with pillar supports on either side.

Now I'm working out the gun cradle geometry, positioning side plates and rails relative to the breech width, checking that trunnion cylinders align with the pivot points, and confirming the muzzle height clears properly at full elevation.

For the capacitors, I'm deciding where they should sit—rejecting a rear deck placement since it conflicts with the breech at full recoil, and instead planning to mount cylindrical capacitors on the turret's sides, stacked vertically with brackets, making sure they stay within the hull's width limits.

I'm adding thin glow rings around the capacitors, placing a warning label on the turret's rear face instead of the sides where it'd get blocked, and routing curved cable sweeps as black tubes connecting the capacitor ends down to the breech.

Now I'm deciding the capacitors and cables should attach to the turret bone so they rotate together rather than staying fixed to the rigid hull, and I'm working out the cab front details—warm-glowing headlight boxes, a dark grille, and a bumper box positioned along the front face near z≈4.5.

I'm adding a diagonal hazard-stripe texture plane on top of the bumper, a visor texture for the windscreen, and small side window planes on the cab sides reusing the same or a separate glass texture. I'm also sizing the cab and hull extrusion widths, then placing a glowing roof lightbar with orange-tipped ends and planning antenna rods extending from the rear roof corners.

Adding sensor turret and exhaust details...

Adding fender flanges with tan-lidded DKOL boxes, then thin side skirts near the wheels, and mudflap boxes positioned behind the rear wheels.

Now I'm placing the rear end details: a bumper box, red-glowing tail lights at either side of the sloped rear deck, and a number plate decal plane centered between them, deciding to skip tow hooks for now.

I'm also figuring out hull side details—vent boxes and emblem placement on the hull sides within the visible band between the deck top and lower hull, making sure these don't clash with wheel fender covers.

I'm thinking about adding a unit number decal to the cab door, then working out the stabilizer legs—positioning the hull-side joints, sizing the support beams, and spacing the legs so they clear the wheel fenders at z=1.65.

Now checking the rear leg placement against the hull boundary and wheel clearance, then figuring out orientation for a hazard warning plane mounted atop the beam—using plane geometry with a custom up-vector so it faces upward along z correctly.

Working out the strut housing and piston cylinder dimensions, brake pad disc, and brace rod positions...

Adding the yellow collar ring, skipping the hose detail for simplicity, and positioning the chassis-level boxes at the hull side and leg root with their dimensions and placement checked against pad footprint clearance.

Now I'm placing the axle details -- diff pumpkins as flattened spheres, iron axle cylinders running along x, and a black driveshaft rod along z -- then checking the under-hull plating skirt and chassis box dimensions so the axles clear the chassis bottom properly. I'm also sketching out the hazard-stripe SVG texture with a yellow rectangle and black diagonal polygons.

Next I'm designing the remaining decal textures: a visor graphic with teal gradient and center divider, an emblem shield with lightning bolt and star, a "DANGER HIGH VOLTAGE" warning label, a plate reading "RG-06", and a door number decal.

I'm also planning hull vent grilles, turret-top greeble like a hatch, periscope, antenna, and sensor pod, then writing the final mirrored construction code using helper functions for parts and glow effects.

For the wheels, I'm designing the tire as a ribbed cylinder, adding a metal rim, a hub dish, and small lug bolts arranged around it.

Still writing wheel placement code...

Adding a rod for the radar antenna mounted on the turret rear, then I'll finalize all the pieces together.
